summary: The SOP provides a structured four-block framework with clear human-in-the-loop guardrails, but it contains critical gaps in cutover write-blocking around CDC drain, broken precheck and post-upgrade verification SQL (including flagging Cloud SQL's built-in cloudsqladmin database as an upgrade blocker), and missing execution steps for index rebuilds and incoming logical subscriptions. In addition, several citations lack supporting quotes in docs/sources.json or rely on a source marked 'changed' without labeling the dependent claims Unverified.

findings.claim: Stopping writers at T-0 relies only on application maintenance mode and a census query without enforcing read-only access at the database level before draining CDC at T+5, allowing stray or scheduled writes between T+5 and T+10 to be permanently lost from CDC consumers when the upgrade deletes all logical replication slots.
findings.evidence: docs/sop.md:247-249 states: '| T-0 | Turn on maintenance mode and stop writers. The census query shows only expected sessions. | App on-call | | / | T+5 | Drain CDC to zero lag and record the LSN | CDC owners | | / | T+10 | Start the upgrade with the rehearsed command | DBA |'. Per S-01 (docs/sources.json:11, https://docs.cloud.google.com/sql/docs/postgres/upgrade-major-db-version-inplace), Cloud SQL's in-place upgrade 'deletes all existing logical replication slots', so any transaction committed after CDC consumers stop at T+5 and before the instance shuts down at T+10 is preserved on the primary but never decoded by either the deleted old slot or the post-upgrade slot created later.
findings.suggested_fix: At T-0, enforce database-level write prevention (for example setting default_transaction_read_only = on or revoking CONNECT/terminating remaining client backends) before draining CDC at T+5, and confirm pg_current_wal_lsn() / transaction IDs do not advance between CDC disconnect and T+10.

findings.claim: The Block 3 cutover starts production CDC consumers and runs smoke tests before 'Go or no-go 2: the point of no return', contradicting the rollback claim that nothing is lost before Go or no-go 2 if CDC consumers have already emitted post-upgrade events or initial snapshots to downstream sinks.
findings.evidence: docs/sop.md:251-256 lists '| Create new slots and start consumers | CDC owners |' before '| Bring up the pooler and routing, then run validation and smoke tests | App on-call | Go or no-go 2: the point of no return |', and then claims under Rollback: 'Before go or no-go 2: restore the pre-upgrade backup to a recovery instance on the source version [S-01], then point the apps back. No writes have happened, so nothing is lost.'
findings.suggested_fix: Create the new logical replication slots before Go or no-go 2 so WAL capture begins immediately, but do not start production downstream CDC sinks (or allow non-read-only smoke tests) until Go or no-go 2 is approved, or explicitly warn that rolling back after starting CDC consumers requires rolling back downstream sinks.

findings.claim: Precheck section 6c flags every non-template0 database with datallowconn = false as a pg_upgrade blocker that must be fixed before exiting Block 1 (G1.1), but every Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL instance has a built-in cloudsqladmin database with datallowconn = false that customers cannot alter or drop.
findings.evidence: plugins/pg-major-upgrade/assets/precheck.sql:162-164 runs: "SELECT datname, datallowconn, datconnlimit FROM pg_database WHERE (datname <> 'template0' AND (NOT datallowconn OR datconnlimit = -2)) OR (datname = 'template0' AND datallowconn);", docs/sop.md:79 states 'Any row in kit section 6a (...), 6b (...), 6c (databases pg_upgrade can\'t connect to) or 6d (...) blocks pg_upgrade 18', and docs/sop.md:114 (G1.1) requires 'Every blocker from G0.3 and G0.4 is fixed in production on the source version, and a rerun of the kit shows it clear | Rerun of kit sections 6a to 6g'.
findings.suggested_fix: Exclude provider-managed internal databases such as 'cloudsqladmin' (and 'rdsadmin' when adapting to RDS) from section 6c in precheck.sql, or document in precheck-reading-guide.md and G1.1 that cloudsqladmin is expected and exempted by Cloud SQL's managed upgrade wrapper.

findings.claim: None of the Block 3 exit gates (G3.1 through G3.4) define required evidence, allowing cutover completion, CDC recovery, 24-hour performance stability, and close-out to be marked Done on someone's say-so.
findings.evidence: docs/sop.md:12 states 'A block exits only when every one of its gate rows in the tracker is Done with linked evidence, or Waived by a named approver' and docs/sop.md:21 states 'each one names the evidence it needs', but docs/sop.md:234-239 defines the Block 3 table with only two columns ('| Gate | Done when |') and omits the 'Evidence' column present in Blocks 0, 1, and 2.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an 'Evidence' column to the Block 3 exit gates table (lines 234-239) specifying verifiable artifacts for G3.1 (validate.sql and smoke test output), G3.2 (slot lag query output and owner sign-off links), G3.3 (24-hour statement latency comparison output), and G3.4 (retro notes, backup retention record, and cleanup verification).

findings.claim: Gate G2.5 requires proving that every CDC consumer resumed from a new slot with no missing or duplicate events, but the Block 2 rehearsal procedure stops writers at step 5 and never generates any pre- or post-upgrade test writes before stopping the clock at step 13.
findings.evidence: docs/sop.md:166 requires 'G2.5 | Every CDC consumer resumed from a new slot with no missing or duplicate events, or a re-snapshot was timed and fits | Consumer check log', while docs/sop.md:183-213 stops writers at step 5 ('Stop writers and drain CDC until the lag is zero'), upgrades at step 7, and says at step 10 'Create new slots and start the test consumer from them. Check that no events are missing or duplicated' without ever executing known sentinel writes before step 5 or after step 10.
findings.suggested_fix: Add explicit steps in Block 2 to insert numbered sentinel rows before step 5 (verifying the last sentinel arrives before drain) and insert post-upgrade sentinel rows after step 10 (verifying the consumer streams them from the new slot with no gaps or duplicates).

findings.claim: The SOP identifies mandatory or recommended post-upgrade REINDEX operations for btree_gist, ltree, full-text search, and pg_trgm indexes on non-libc clusters, as well as PK/FK collation constraints in PG 18, but omits them from Block 1 tasks, Block 2 rehearsal timings, and the Block 3 cutover runbook.
findings.evidence: docs/sop.md:86 states 'Indexes using btree_gist\'s float4 or float8 operator classes, or ltree, may need a reindex after 14.24 [S-21]', and docs/sop.md:307-308 lists '18 | Full-text search and pg_trgm indexes need a reindex on non-libc clusters | DBA, if ICU or builtin | S-17' and '18 | PK and FK pairs must use deterministic or matching nondeterministic collations | DBA, if nondeterministic collations | S-17' (citing S-17, https://www.postgresql.org/docs/18/release-18.html, quotes in docs/sources.json:241-242). However, neither Block 1 (lines 125-138), Block 2 (lines 171-215), nor Block 3 (lines 244-254) includes a task or step to check PK/FK collations or run and time REINDEX.
findings.suggested_fix: Add queries to precheck.sql to detect non-libc (ICU/builtin) full-text search/pg_trgm indexes and mismatched/nondeterministic PK/FK collations, add a Block 1 fix task for PK/FK collations and reindex scripts, and add an explicit REINDEX timing and execution step to Blocks 2 and 3.

findings.claim: Block 2 step 5 (and Block 3 T+5) instructs operators to wait until pg_wal_lsn_diff(pg_current_wal_lsn(), confirmed_flush_lsn) reaches zero across pg_replication_slots, which returns NULL for physical slots and rarely reaches zero on Cloud SQL because background system writes advance pg_current_wal_lsn() ahead of database-scoped logical slots.
findings.evidence: docs/sop.md:183-188 states: '5. Start the window clock. Stop writers and drain CDC until the lag is zero: SELECT slot_name, pg_wal_lsn_diff(pg_current_wal_lsn(), confirmed_flush_lsn) AS lag_bytes FROM pg_replication_slots;' and docs/sop.md:248 states 'T+5 | Drain CDC to zero lag and record the LSN'. In PostgreSQL, pg_replication_slots includes physical slots where confirmed_flush_lsn is NULL, and logical slots only advance confirmed_flush_lsn on decoded commits while background checkpoints or Cloud SQL internal heartbeats advance pg_current_wal_lsn().
findings.suggested_fix: Filter the query by WHERE slot_type = 'logical', and instruct operators to verify that all application writes are stopped, confirmed_flush_lsn has stopped advancing across two consecutive checks, and pg_stat_replication sent_lsn/flush_lsn match rather than waiting for pg_wal_lsn_diff(pg_current_wal_lsn(), confirmed_flush_lsn) = 0.

findings.claim: Gate G2.3, Block 2 steps 3 and 9, and Block 3 close-out require that 'every table has planner stats' and use pg_stats row existence to find unanalyzed tables, which fails whenever a database has empty tables, all-NULL tables, or tables owned by roles other than the database owner.
findings.evidence: docs/sop.md:164 requires 'G2.3 | After the upgrade every table has planner stats, or the analyze step covers the gap inside the window | Stats counts before and after', docs/sop.md:194-205 runs 'SELECT c.oid::regclass AS table_name FROM pg_class c ... WHERE ... NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pg_stats s WHERE s.schemaname = n.nspname AND s.tablename = c.relname)' as 'the database owner, because ANALYZE silently skips tables the caller can\'t analyze [S-16]', and docs/sop.md:261 says 'Confirm no table lacks stats.' Per S-16 (https://www.postgresql.org/docs/18/sql-analyze.html, docs/sources.json:223), ANALYZE requires table ownership or MAINTAIN privilege (not database ownership), and PostgreSQL never creates pg_statistic/pg_stats rows for zero-row or all-NULL tables even after ANALYZE.
findings.suggested_fix: Run ANALYZE and stats checks in every database as a role with privileges across all user table owners (such as cloudsqlsuperuser on Cloud SQL), exclude empty tables (reltuples = 0 and pg_relation_size(c.oid) = 0) from the missing-stats query, and check pg_stat_all_tables.last_analyze for cumulative stats verification.

findings.claim: Source S-10 is marked 'changed' in docs/sources.md and docs/sources.json, which by the template's own rules makes every claim citing S-10 Unverified, yet docs/sop.md and precheck-reading-guide.md present S-10 claims without an Unverified label or a settlement question.
findings.evidence: docs/sources.md:3 states: 'A source whose quotes have moved is marked changed, and one that can\'t be fetched is marked unreachable. Treat claims that cite it as Unverified until someone rechecks.' docs/sources.md:25 and docs/sources.json:148 mark S-10 as 'changed' ('status': 'changed'). However, docs/sop.md:87 ('Cloud SQL maintenance installs new binaries but doesn\'t update extension versions [S-10]'), docs/sop.md:192 ('run ALTER EXTENSION ... UPDATE for each pending extension [S-10]'), and plugins/pg-major-upgrade/skills/pg-upgrade-precheck/references/precheck-reading-guide.md:58 cite [S-10] as verified without flagging it Unverified.
findings.suggested_fix: Either re-verify S-10 against https://docs.cloud.google.com/sql/docs/postgres/extensions and update its quotes and status in docs/sources.json, or label all S-10 claims in docs/sop.md and precheck-reading-guide.md as Unverified and state how the rehearsal settles them.

findings.claim: Claims labeled Verified with [S-22], [S-18], and [S-05] in docs/sop.md are not fully supported by the quote lists for those sources in docs/sources.json.
findings.evidence: docs/sop.md:79 states 'Any row in kit section 6a (reg* types, aclitem, system composite types), 6b (prepared transactions), 6c (databases pg_upgrade can\'t connect to) or 6d (child columns missing a parent NOT NULL) blocks pg_upgrade 18. All four are Verified in pg_upgrade\'s own checks [S-22]', but S-22 in docs/sources.json:312-318 has no quote for system composite types or datallowconn/unconnectable databases. Similarly, docs/sop.md:81 cites [S-18] for 'db_user_namespace and trace_recovery_messages', which are absent from S-18's quotes in docs/sources.json:254-259, and docs/sop.md:98 cites [S-05] for 'nobody can read pg_authid [S-05]' while docs/sources.md:19 cites S-05 for 'doesn\'t include pg_statistic', neither of which appears in S-05's quotes in docs/sources.json:77-80.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the exact supporting quotes from pg_upgrade's check.c (S-22), the PG 17 release notes (S-18), and Cloud SQL's users page (S-05) into docs/sources.json, or relabel unsupported claims as Inferred.

findings.claim: While precheck.sql queries inbound logical replication subscriptions (pg_subscription and pglogical.subscription), the SOP omits inbound subscriptions from G0.5, Block 1 preparation, Block 2 rehearsal, and Block 3 cutover steps.
findings.evidence: plugins/pg-major-upgrade/assets/precheck.sql:96 runs 'SELECT subname, subenabled FROM pg_subscription;' and line 238 runs 'SELECT sub_name, sub_enabled, sub_slot_name FROM pglogical.subscription;', and plugins/pg-major-upgrade/skills/pg-upgrade-precheck/references/precheck-reading-guide.md:41 notes 'Subscriptions mean this instance also consumes from somewhere.' However, docs/sop.md:41 (G0.5), line 55 (B0-07), line 131 (B1-05), and the Block 2/3 runbooks address only outbound slots, publications, and pglogical nodes, never disabling, upgrading, or re-enabling subscriptions where this instance is a subscriber.
findings.suggested_fix: Include pg_subscription and pglogical.subscription in G0.5 and B0-07, and add runbook steps in Blocks 2 and 3 to disable inbound subscriptions before the upgrade, verify subscription metadata/replication origins after the upgrade, and re-enable them.

findings.claim: Precheck section 5b lists only schema and table names of unlogged tables without showing whether an unlogged table is partitioned or has generated columns, and Gate G1.1 omits section 5b and section 3 when verifying that upgrade blockers are cleared.
findings.evidence: docs/sop.md:93-94 warns that 'PG 18 refuses unlogged partitioned tables [S-17]' and 'Cloud SQL warns that unlogged tables with generated columns fail with unexpected request for new relfilenumber in binary upgrade mode [S-01]'. However, plugins/pg-major-upgrade/assets/precheck.sql:115-117 only runs "SELECT n.nspname, c.relname FROM pg_class c JOIN pg_namespace n ON n.oid = c.relnamespace WHERE c.relpersistence = 'u' AND c.relkind IN ('r','p');" without outputting c.relkind or checking pg_attribute.attgenerated, and docs/sop.md:114 (G1.1) only reruns 'kit sections 6a to 6g' to prove blockers are fixed.
findings.suggested_fix: Include c.relkind and an EXISTS check for pg_attribute.attgenerated <> '' in precheck.sql section 5b, classify unlogged partitioned tables and unlogged tables with generated columns as G0.4 blockers in precheck-reading-guide.md, and include sections 3 and 5b in the G1.1 verification rerun.

findings.claim: Precheck section 6a checks only c.relkind IN ('r','m','i') for banned column types (reg*, aclitem, system composite), missing partitioned parent tables (relkind = 'p') that have no leaf partitions yet, and section 6g misses functions called via regular views underlying materialized views or in generated columns and CHECK constraints.
findings.evidence: plugins/pg-major-upgrade/assets/precheck.sql:153 filters 'AND c.relkind IN (\'r\',\'m\',\'i\')', whereas pg_upgrade's check_for_data_types_usage in check.c (S-22, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/postgres/postgres/REL_18_STABLE/src/bin/pg_upgrade/check.c) also checks RELKIND_PARTITIONED_TABLE ('p'). In addition, precheck.sql:196-199 only checks direct pg_depend links from indexes or materialized views (m.relkind = 'm'), missing functions without a pinned search_path invoked through intermediate views (relkind = 'v'), generated columns, or CHECK constraints during PG 17+ maintenance operations [S-18].
findings.suggested_fix: Add 'p' to c.relkind IN ('r','m','p','i') in precheck.sql line 153, and expand section 6g to recursively traverse view and function dependencies as well as pg_constraint (CHECK constraints) and pg_attrdef (generated columns).

findings.claim: The SOP links to tracker-schema.md for gate and tracker row definitions and to ../plugins/pg-major-upgrade/ for guardrail rules and hooks, but neither exists in the reviewed artifacts and the required schema for tracker rows is not defined inline.
findings.evidence: docs/sop.md:21 states 'Gate rows live in the tracker ([tracker-schema.md](tracker-schema.md)), and each one names the evidence it needs' and docs/sop.md:279 states 'These are enforced by [the plugin\'s rules and hook](../plugins/pg-major-upgrade/).' Neither docs/tracker-schema.md nor any rules/hooks under plugins/pg-major-upgrade/ are present under review/.
findings.suggested_fix: Include docs/tracker-schema.md and the referenced plugin rules/hooks in the artifact set, or define the required columns for Consumer, CDC, Role, Question, and Gate rows directly in docs/sop.md.

findings.claim: Section 6 (Logical branch) states that it replaces Block 2 steps 4 to 12, which drops essential post-promotion steps including extension updates, running ANALYZE, recreating downstream CDC slots on the new primary, running validation scripts and plan diffs, and checking pooler/replica routing, while leaving Block 3 hardcoded to an in-place upgrade.
findings.evidence: docs/sop.md:268 states 'Use this only if the decision record picks a logical migration. It replaces Block 2 steps 4 to 12.' Replacing steps 4 to 12 removes step 8 (version and extension checks), step 9 (ANALYZE), step 10 (downstream CDC slot recreation), step 11 (validation scripts, smoke tests, and top-statement plan diffs), and step 12 (pooler and replica routing), and Block 3 (lines 248-253) still specifies in-place steps rather than logical promotion, sequence verification, and connection switchover.
findings.suggested_fix: Have Section 6 replace only the data-transfer and cutover mechanics (Block 2 steps 6-7) while keeping CDC drain, ANALYZE, downstream slot creation, sequence verification, validation scripts, and routing checks, and add a logical cutover sequence to Block 3.

findings.claim: Gate G1.1 claims to verify that every blocker from both G0.3 (provider precheck) and G0.4 (precheck kit) is fixed in production, but its required evidence only reruns kit sections 6a to 6g and does not rerun the provider precheck.
findings.evidence: docs/sop.md:114 states: '| G1.1 | Every blocker from G0.3 and G0.4 is fixed in production on the source version, and a rerun of the kit shows it clear | Rerun of kit sections 6a to 6g |', whereas G0.3 (line 39) is the provider precheck ('Precheck JSON and operations describe JSON').
findings.suggested_fix: Require a clean rerun of the provider precheck (gcloud sql instances pre-check-major-version-upgrade and operations describe) alongside kit sections 3, 5b, and 6a-6g as evidence for G1.1.

findings.claim: Cloud SQL-specific restrictions from S-05 and S-01/S-08 are stated as if they applied to all managed services or all providers, and Section 8 omits several Cloud SQL-specific steps when adapting to another provider.
findings.evidence: docs/sop.md:98 states 'On managed services nobody can read pg_authid [S-05]' and line 195 states 'managed services don\'t give customers superuser [S-05]', citing a Cloud SQL-only page (https://docs.cloud.google.com/sql/docs/postgres/users). Additionally, Section 8 (lines 285-291) omits G0.3's 'operations describe JSON' (line 39) and Block 2/3's assumption that the upgrade deletes all logical slots (lines 190, 208, 251), even though vanilla pg_upgrade from PG 17+ preserves logical slots [S-14, S-22].
findings.suggested_fix: Qualify lines 98 and 195 as Cloud SQL (or managed Postgres services that restrict superuser access), and update Section 8 to include G0.3 evidence artifacts and logical slot preservation rules when adapting to other providers.

findings.claim: Appendix B question 4 ('Does an upgrade that includes replicas keep each replica\'s stats and hostname?') is marked Unverified in Appendix B, but is never flagged in the SOP body or tested on replicas during the Block 2 rehearsal.
findings.evidence: docs/sop.md:315-320 states 'These are Unverified until the provider answers or the rehearsal shows the answer. ... 4. Does an upgrade that includes replicas keep each replica\'s stats and hostname?', but Block 2 step 2 (line 175), step 9 (line 194, which only checks stats on the primary), and step 12 (line 211) never record or compare replica hostnames or replica planner stats before and after the rehearsal upgrade.
findings.suggested_fix: Label replica hostname and planner-stats preservation as Unverified in Block 2 steps 2, 9, and 12, and add a rehearsal check that records replica connection endpoints and pg_stats counts on each replica before and after the upgrade.

findings.claim: The precheck reading guide evaluates sections 2d (relation count) and 2e (large object count) against Cloud SQL's instance-wide limits (100,000 relations and 10 million large objects) without instructing the reader to sum those counts across all per-database precheck-<db>.txt files.
findings.evidence: plugins/pg-major-upgrade/skills/pg-upgrade-precheck/references/precheck-reading-guide.md:12 notes that 'Sections 2b to 2e, 5, 6 and 8 run per database', but lines 37-38 state for section 2d 'The sum is well under 100,000 | Cloud SQL is tuned for up to about 100,000 relations [S-01]' and for section 2e 'large_objects = 0 | More than 10 million large objects fails the MVU [S-01]' without noting that the per-database outputs must be summed across every database on the instance.
findings.suggested_fix: Clarify in precheck-reading-guide.md lines 37-38 and 67 that sections 2d and 2e are per-database catalog queries whose counts must be summed across all databases on the instance before comparing against Cloud SQL's 100,000-relation and 10-million-large-object instance limits.
